tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk you need to move is not the topmost on its peg, you must first relocate any smaller disks that sit above it. This clears the larger disk so it can be moved legally.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that has smaller disks on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempted to move disk 5 while disk 2 was still on top of it, resulting in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before issuing a move, check that the disk you intend to move is actually the topmost disk on its source peg. Moving a non‑top disk violates the Tower of Hanoi rules.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Tried to move disk 5 from peg 1 while disk 3 was on top, causing a source‑top mismatch.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the destination peg is either empty or its topmost disk is larger than the moving disk. Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one is illegal.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moved disk 4 onto peg 2 where disk 2 was on top, violating size ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To transfer a contiguous stack of k disks from one peg to another, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the kth (largest) disk to the target, then move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you have a clean stack of consecutive disks on a peg and need to move the whole stack to another peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempted to move a stack of disks without recursively clearing the smaller ones first, leading to illegal placements.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear destination peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk onto a target peg, make sure the target does not have any smaller disks on top, because they would block the larger disk's placement.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you are about to place a larger disk onto a peg that already contains disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moved disk 5 onto peg 2 while disk 1 was on top, making the move illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate final configuration after move generation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, simulate the moves from the initial state and compare the resulting configuration with the goal. This catches any missed illegal moves or missing steps.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have generated the full move list, before outputting it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Generated a move list that left disk 3 on peg 0 instead of the goal peg, causing the final configuration to be wrong.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use the smallest disk as a flexible temporary placeholder
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any larger disk or an empty peg without restriction, making it a useful temporary holder while you free larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need to free a larger disk but have no empty peg, move the smallest disk onto a larger one to create space.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Failed to move the smallest disk to a temporary peg, causing a deadlock when trying to free a larger disk.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Place move list as the final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Output the move list as the last list in the response and avoid any additional brackets, code fences, or text after it, so the parser reads the correct list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Added extra explanatory text after the move list, causing the parser to read an empty or wrong list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Keep move list concise to avoid token limit truncation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate a short, near‑optimal sequence (e.g., by using recursion for sub‑stacks) rather than an overly long list, to stay within the token limit and avoid truncation.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the move list, aim for minimal or near‑minimal length.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Produced a very long move list that was cut off by the token limit, resulting in an incomplete solution.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop generation early or forget to produce the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always generate at least one move; if the initial state already matches the goal, output an empty list explicitly, otherwise ensure the move list is produced.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model generates too many moves or extra text, causing the output to be cut off by the system's token limit.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep the move list concise, limit the number of moves, and avoid extra explanatory text after the list.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model does not check the current top of the source peg before issuing a move.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the disk to be moved is the topmost disk on its source peg before adding the move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal placement)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model fails to verify that the destination peg's top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk before moving.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Extra list after move list causing parser to read wrong answer
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model adds explanations or additional formatting after the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Place the move list as the very last list in the response and avoid any further brackets or code fences.
